source.locator: Theorem 1 specialized to fourth moments; standardized notation is reproduced in Fan and Shao (2018), Introduction, equations (2)--(3)

attestation.note: The stable DOI and exact theorem locator are supplied in lieu of a verbatim transcription.  The exponent and the two error terms were cross-checked against the open reproduction in arXiv:1712.03667, equations (2)--(3), at moment parameter two.

proposed.justification: This quantitative consequence follows from the verified rank-indexed martingale, prefix-flip bounds, and the cited fourth-moment martingale normal-approximation theorem.
proposed.gap: Theorem 5.6 of \cite{KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024CGD} requires \(d=o(n^{1/9})\); the new proof uses the exact forward filtration and its concentrated predictable quadratic variation.
proposed.consumer: Future CGD replications can check the graph-degree growth rule before replacing conservative Chebyshev calibration by a normal critical value.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Add the theorem-granular Heyde--Brown fourth-moment martingale inequality as the declared imported dependency used by the proof.

proposed.justification: The repeated-star calculation supplies a legal critical compound limit under the original endpoint fourth moments and variance floor.
proposed.gap: Proposition 5.8 of \cite{KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024CGD} alternates a single star with another graph and does not locate the worst-case degree boundary.
proposed.consumer: The construction supplies necessity for degree envelopes that are not \(o(n^{2/3})\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the theorem-granular martingale normal approximation used for the independent leaf-label component of the boundary limit.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The exact constant-order expression for \(\mathcal R_n(d;B,c)\) when \(d=o(n^{2/3})\), including a legal CGD lower array matching each dominant normal-approximation term.
open_obligations.obstruction: The verified Heyde--Brown bound has the generic martingale exponent \(1/5\), but its known sharpness examples are not shown to be representable by the constrained CGD prefix-product increments.  The repeated-star family proves a non-Gaussian critical boundary but does not match the vanishing \(1/5\)-power upper rate in the subcritical regime.
open_obligations.attempted: The forward Doob decomposition, the shared-parent flip envelope, the spectral operator chain, and the repeated-star hub-count perturbation were all derived.  They close the convergence frontier, but no CGD endpoint and graph array obtained from these constructions matches the generic martingale rate throughout the interior regime.
